messages:
maya: Heads-up — since ~05:10 UTC we're seeing a bunch of GPU provisioning failures in us-west2. Pods stay Pending, kube scheduler logs show NodeSelectors matched but pods get stuck with ImagePull/attach timeouts. i/o metrics on the nodes show NVMe IOPS spikes and high write latencies.

infra-bot: [ALERT] cluster-us-west2: node-group-gpu-3 reported nvme_write_latency > 250ms (5m avg). Affected: 8 nodes.

sam: Confirmed. Ephemeral-cleaner started a full scrub sweep after the recent firmware rollout; concurrency jumped to 16 for the cleaner job and scrub workers saturated local NVMe. iostat from one host: ```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           12.3    0.0    8.1   45.6     0.0    34.0
Device            r/s    w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         150.0  1200.5  10240.0  98304.0  80.0     40.2   230.6  18.5   212.1  1.2   98.3
```

lee: Oof. That avgqu-sz/await is the culprit. Cleaner shouldn't be able to push the queue that high during business hours — it starves kubelet attach/detach and pod provisioning times out.

natalie: Quick cost question: if we throttle the cleaner we'll push scrub backlog longer and possibly increase wear? what's the tradeoff?

sam: Throttling reduces instantaneous writes so short-term wear goes down; backlog means more total bytes over time but spread out. Main tradeoff is GPU provisioning latency / eviction risk vs. deferred cleanup. For now availability trumps immediate GC.

ash: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) scale cleaner concurrency to 2 on affected nodepool via ConfigMap. 2) Add a node-alloc taint so new GPU pods avoid nodes currently scrubbing. 3) Temporarily bump Dedicated capacity (reserve 2 extra nodes in us-west2) so scheduler can place pods.

maya: I'm going to push a hotfix: update daemonset ENV CLEANER_MAX_WORKERS=2 and set SCRUB_RATE_LIMIT=50MB/s. Patching now.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: rolling-update daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner -> image:infra/ephemeral-cleaner:v2026.03.18-hotfix started.

sam: Patch applied to node-group-gpu-3, monitoring shows write IOPS down ~70% and nvme_write_latency falling to ~40ms after 3 minutes. Provisioning failures reduced.

lee: Can we add a longer-term safeguard? Proposal: enforce IO QoS via cgroups on cleaner, and a scheduler predicate that deprioritizes nodes with scrub_backlog>100GB for new GPU pods.

natalie: Also add a cost estimate for bumping Dedicated capacity for 48h (SRE + finance) — short-term cost vs. customer-facing throttling impact. I'll chase number.

ash: I'll open infra ticket and link runbook updates: set default cleaner concurrency to 4, add night-only full-sweep window, and expose per-node scrub_backlog metric to console.

maya: tl;dr: hotfix reduced latency/provisioning failures. Next steps: ticket + runbook + QA on IO QoS. Will follow up with rollback window. :thumbsup:
